data.body:
CLOSE BLOCKED — and my own AC was false. Recording both.

The completion verifier FAILED this ticket, on the criterion asserting rebar-autodeploy-errors
was OK with deploy_errors 0.0 across the preceding 30 minutes. The verifier was RIGHT and I was
wrong: a 5-minute-period query straddled a deploy_errors = 2.0 at 07:12Z. I reported a green
reading from a window that happened to miss the failure. That criterion is corrected and
REOPENED; this ticket does not close on a claim I cannot support.

Worth naming separately: the alarm being OK is not evidence of healthy deploys here.
rebar-autodeploy-errors is Sum over 900s requiring 3-of-4 datapoints with notBreaching on
missing data, so an ISOLATED deploy failure cannot trip it by construction. I had been treating
that green alarm as confirmation.

The deeper reason this ticket cannot yet be closed: the fix merged at 06:47Z (30d7059f632d) is
NOT RUNNING on the box. Root cause filed as carefree-swift-scallop — autodeploy.sh:541 exits 0
on a review-bot deferral, so the mcp blue-green block at :616 (which documents itself as
INDEPENDENT of the bot block) is never reached. A shared src/rebar change matches BOTH triggers,
so a busy bot silently skips the mcp deploy. Live probe confirms it: the deployed server still
returns the OLD behaviour.

There is a circularity here that is worth stating plainly, because it bounds what this ticket
can achieve on its own: THIS ticket's fix is the mcp deploy fix, and it cannot deploy because of
carefree-swift-scallop. And my own push volume is part of the chain — saturating the
single-worker review bot keeps in_flight > 0, which is what keeps autodeploy deferring.

This ticket stays in_progress until the merged fix is confirmed RUNNING, not merely merged.
